response.title: Do I need a separate solar charge controller between my solar panels and a portable power station?
response.answer:
No, in most cases you do not need a separate solar charge controller between your solar panels and a portable power station.

Most modern portable power stations, such as those from EcoFlow, Jackery, Bluetti, and Anker SOLIX, have a built-in MPPT solar charge controller.

How the connection works

Typical setup: direct connection

What you need to check

Before connecting your panels, verify these specifications:

Specification

	

What matters




Solar input voltage

	

Panel array's maximum open-circuit voltage (Voc), including cold-weather increases, must stay below the station's limit




Solar input current

	

Check the station's maximum input current and connector ratings




Solar input wattage

	

Determines how much solar power the station can accept




Connector

	

Must be compatible (e.g., MC4 to XT60) and correctly polarized

When would you need an external charge controller?

An external controller is generally used when charging a standalone battery directly, rather than a portable power station with an integrated solar controller.

Important: Adding an external MPPT controller in front of a power station's solar input is generally unnecessary and can cause compatibility problems. It also does not safely bypass the station's voltage limits.

I can check your exact setup

Tell me these two things:

Portable power station brand and model (e.g., EcoFlow DELTA 2, Bluetti AC200L).

Solar panel specifications (wattage, Voc, Vmp, and number of panels).

I'll tell you whether you can connect them directly, whether you should wire the panels in series or parallel, and whether you need any additional equipment.
